items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: AC1-AC6 each implemented and tested; AC3 satisfied by placement rather than a documented exception after the first design was found to be unreachable on the real path.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Fail-soft by design and never silent: refresh failure, stage failure and restore failure each append their own step the caller returns. check=False everywhere in the post-merge window, per the module contract that nothing there may raise.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No network, no secrets, no user input. Only new surface is reading an already-committed ADR folder and writing one file inside it.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: 5 tests, all real-git through the actual integrate_main.integrate with no stubbed regenerator. The stage-failure fix was mutation-checked (replacing the restore with pass turns it RED). One test that passed with the feature reverted was DELETED rather than patched.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: One extra folder scan per integrate merge; negligible against the git and network work already in that phase.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: Placement moved to integrate_regenerate after the bloat gate showed resolve_churn_conflicts.py sits exactly at its ADR-099 ceiling; churn_merge.py trimmed 300 -> 297 so headroom is restored rather than consumed.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: Registry <-> doc table (doc-sync 1:1 both directions) and the producer/consumer pair, corrected after Stage 1 caught the row naming an abandoned consumer. That table is machine-parsed into the compliance artifact, so a false row would have shipped a false traceability record.

items.name: Test Hygiene Probe
items.note: No skips, no xfails. cross_component fires on this diff, so the F11 integration-coverage gate applies and is satisfied by a category:integration behavior. UTF-8 forced on git reads (cp1252 mangles the em-dash in every index row).
